sxsw-2026-what-actually-matters-right-no.prose_html:
I’ve just come back from SXSW in Austin.

We were part of the UK delegation, one of 18 companies selected to represent British creative and tech capability. A genuine privilege, and a useful lens for seeing where things are heading.

But beyond the scale, the noise, and the spectacle, a few things stood out.

AI isn’t replacing creativity. It’s exposing it.

AI was everywhere, as expected.

But the more interesting conversation wasn’t about what it can do. It was about what happens when everyone has access to the same tools.

The output starts to converge.

Which makes one thing very clear.
Good enough is becoming the default.

If you’re relying on AI alone, you’ll likely land somewhere in the middle. Safe, predictable, and forgettable.

The opportunity isn’t in using AI.
It’s in directing it well.

That still requires:

  • taste
  • judgement
  • experience
  • and a clear point of view

If anything, creativity has become more valuable, not less.

The real gap is not capability. It’s confidence.

There’s a lot of experimentation happening.

Teams are building quickly, prototyping faster than ever, and exploring what’s possible.

But underneath that, there’s a noticeable tension:

  • Is what we’ve built reliable?
  • Is it secure?
  • What happens when it breaks?
  • Do we actually understand it?

The technology is moving fast.
Confidence in using it well is not.

That gap is where experienced partners become critical.

The role of agencies is shifting

A lot of agencies were there, both UK and US.

And the conversation is changing.

Less about execution.
More about guidance, structure, and clarity.

Because when everything speeds up, poor decisions compound faster.

The value is no longer just in making things.

It’s in helping teams:

  • make better decisions
  • prioritise what matters
  • avoid expensive missteps

Innovation is real, but uneven

From robotics to self-driving vehicles to AI in healthcare, the pace of change is undeniable.

Even small moments, like robots serving coffee, make it tangible.

But it’s not consistent.

Some companies are moving with clarity.
Others are chasing trends without a clear use case.

The difference is strategy.

Relationships still matter more than anything

Despite all the technology, the most valuable part of the week was still people.

Conversations with companies like Mastercard, BBC, and others across different sectors reinforced the same thing.

Opportunities don’t come from tools.
They come from shared understanding and trust.

And SXSW is still one of the best places to build that.

Final thought

There’s a lot of noise right now.

New tools. New possibilities. New pressure to move faster.

But the fundamentals haven’t changed.

If anything, they’ve become clearer:

  1. Creativity matters more
  2. Strategy matters more
  3. Experience matters more

AI is accelerating everything.

But it’s not replacing the need for thinking.

reinventing-forms-with-a-travel-ai-agent.prose_html:
Forms have long been a staple of digital experiences, but let’s be honest they’re often boring. Whether it’s a product configurator, a sign-up flow, or a service wizard, filling out forms can quickly become a chore.

We’ve been exploring a concept that brings a fresh take to this experience by combining two modern interface techniques: AI agents (also referred to as human interfaces) and traditional user interfaces.

Instead of just presenting a static form, this approach uses a hybrid model: a conversational AI agent guides the user, while visual UI elements present clear options. The result is a more dynamic, human-like interaction layered with visual support, helping users better understand their choices in an intuitive way.

By weaving together conversation and visuals, the experience becomes:

  • More engaging. It feels like a dialogue, not a data entry session.
  • More accessible. With voice recognition and voice controls, users can navigate using speech, opening the experience to a wider audience.
  • More conversational. The AI agent can adapt to user responses, offering a sense of flow and personalization that traditional forms simply can’t match.

To show how this can work in practice, we created a unique demo focused on the travel industry.

You can watch it here:

Watch the Travel AI Agent demo

In this concept, a digital travel agent chats with you about your preferences, from dream destinations to favorite activities, while a visual interface displays suggestions and choices. By the end of the conversation, you’re presented with a curated list of holiday ideas tailored to your interests.

The possibilities don’t stop at travel. This hybrid model could be adapted to many industries, wherever choice, personalization, and accessibility are key to a better customer experience.

5-figma-features-i-couldnt-live-without.prose_html:
It’s no secret that Figma is an incredibly powerful design software. Even though we use it each and every day, there are new features being added constantly so we are always adapting the way we work to stay up to date. But what are the features I couldn’t live without? Well, in reality, the list is far too long to go through each and every one. So here’s my top five:

Creating Styles

Consistency is key when it comes to branding. The nature of what we do means that we are constantly working with different brands and being able to apply these properly to our designs is so important. Our starting point with almost any project is a design system; a way of working that would be impossible without the styles feature. We create a library of colours, fonts and effects that are then used across every aspect of our designs. Not only is this a massive time-saver, but it also allows us to rest easy knowing that, should there be any changes, we can update the style and apply that change to everything we have done so far. Believe me, you don’t want to be updating a HEX code manually across an entire website design.

Components

In a similar way to styles being applied to our designs, creating components allows us to build a bank of reusable assets. Whether it’s a small item, such as a button (we call these atoms), or a larger more complex element, like a product card (we call these molecules), if it appears more than once in our designs we aim to create a component for it. This then allows us to apply updates globally and make sure everything stays consistent. Within a component, we can then create ‘variants’ to show how it should look in different states or circumstances. Not to mention being able to set interactions and prototype these elements… which leads me nicely to the next feature.

Prototyping

Explaining interactions, hover states & scroll behaviour to clients or developers can sometimes be a painful experience for both parties. And yet it’s the part of a project that can really bring the designs to life. That’s why prototyping definitely needs to feature on this list. Whether it’s a hover effect for a button or creating a fully functioning website prototype, we can show exactly how we think these things should work. Right down to the detail of transition speed and style.. it never gets old. And then there’s presentation mode, a view where the designs can be shown on a mockup device with the full interactivity on display. Sometimes the only problem is explaining to clients that their website still needs to be built!

Comments

Maybe just as important as the other features mentioned already are the comments. Feedback on designs can sometimes be difficult to interpret and manage. However, this can be made easier by allowing people to add a comment to the specific part of the design they are referencing. Avoiding the confusion of trying to figure out where their feedback is relating to. And then once the comment is addressed, it can be responded to or marked as resolved to keep the paper trail going. Sounds simple, but at times this can be a lifesaver.

The Shortcuts

Last but not least, it’s the keyboard shortcuts. And yes, I know just about every piece of software has them and it’s nothing new. But with the sheer scale of what can be done in Figma, I couldn’t live without them. Being able to quickly navigate to the right frame or perform a repetitive action in seconds creates huge efficiencies. The old cliche of working smarter, not harder really does apply here. Sure, you could find everything you need in the menus but how long is that going to take? Now this isn’t something you can pick up and benefit from overnight. Far from it. The starting point involves a lot of ‘ahh how do I do that again?’ and frantic googling, but when you do this every day things really start to click.. literally. 

So that’s five Figma Features I couldn’t live without. I could ramble on for days about the finer details but the truth is, Figma is an industry leader for a reason. Adopting the best tools equips us to do the best work and that’s what we love. Do you agree with my picks or would your list look a little different?

ux-design-vs-seo.prose_html:
UX Design and SEO are two important aspects of website development and digital marketing. Although they have different goals, both UX design and SEO are crucial for the success of a website.

UX Design, or User Experience Design, is the process of creating products, systems, or services that provide meaningful and relevant experiences to users. This includes designing the interface, layout, navigation, and overall user experience of a website. The main goal of UX design is to make sure that users have a positive and productive experience when they interact with the website.

designing-for-e-commerce-stores.prose_html:
Here’s a few ideas to make sure the your store performs better and has every chance for conversion.

  1. Keep the website design simple and easy to navigate, with a clear hierarchy of information.
  2. Use high-quality images and videos to showcase products.
  3. Make the checkout process as quick and easy as possible, with minimal required information.
  4. Use clear and prominent calls to action, such as “Add to Cart” or “Buy Now.”
  5. Use A/B testing to find the best design and layout for your website.
  6. Use trust symbols, such as security badges, to build trust and increase conversions.
  7. Optimise the website for mobile devices, as more and more users are shopping on their smartphones.
  8. Make it easy for customers to contact you with questions or concerns, and respond quickly to inquiries.
  9. Use personalised recommendations and product suggestions based on browsing history and purchase history.
  10. Use exit-intent pop-ups to capture email addresses from leaving visitors, making sure you stand out ahead of competitors.
  11. Clearly define and communicate your unique value proposition, highlighting what sets your products or services apart from competitors.
  12. Develop a strong brand identity, including a consistent visual style and messaging across all marketing channels.
  13. Leverage customer testimonials, reviews, and social proof to build trust and credibility.
  14. Use targeted marketing to reach the specific customer segments you want to attract.
  15. Use storytelling and emotional appeals to connect with customers on a deeper level.
  16. Focus on building a strong online presence, including a website optimised for conversions and active social media accounts.
  17. Use SEO and paid advertising to increase visibility and drive traffic to your website.
  18. Offer exceptional customer service, and go above and beyond to create a memorable customer experience.
  19. Create high-quality, informative content such as blog posts, ebooks, webinars, and videos to educate your customers and establish yourself as an authority in your industry.
  20. Create loyalty and reward programs to incentivise frequent purchases and build long-term customer relationships.

how-ai-could-affect-digital-design.prose_html:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionise the field of digital design, making the design process faster, more efficient, and more accurate.

One way that AI could affect digital design is through the use of generative design algorithms. These algorithms can generate a wide range of design options based on a set of input parameters and constraints, allowing designers to quickly explore many possibilities and find the best solution for their needs.

Another way that AI could impact digital design is through the use of machine learning algorithms, which can be trained to recognize patterns and make predictions about how users will interact with a design. This can help designers create more intuitive and user-friendly designs better suited to their target audience.

AI can also be used to automate repetitive and time-consuming tasks, such as image editing and optimization. This can free up designers to focus on more creative and strategic tasks, such as brainstorming new ideas and experimenting with new design concepts.

AI-assisted design tools are also emerging that can help generate website layouts, design logos, generate colour schemes and even create animations.

However, it’s important to note that AI is not a replacement for human designers, but rather a tool that can enhance their work and help them create better designs more efficiently. The designer’s role will continue to be critical, as they are responsible for guiding the AI’s output and ensuring that the final design meets the needs of the user.

In conclusion, AI has the potential to greatly impact digital design and change the way we design digital products. It has the ability to streamline the process and help us create more efficient and user-friendly designs. However, it’s important to remember that AI will not replace human designers but augment their work.
